article.title: How to Practice “Leave no Trace”

bodies.content:
What is Leave no Trace? The general idea of Leave no Trace is to sustain the environment for generations to come while doing outdoor activities like camping or hiking  by following these 7 principles.



    1. Plan Ahead and Prepare




    • Do adequate research on the area you are visiting

 

    • Always be prepared for any weather conditions

 

    • Repackage food to minimize waste




    1. Travel and Camp on durable surfaces




    • Camp on nearby water sources like lakes and streams

 

    • Keep the campsite minimalistic and small




    1. Dispose of waste properly




    • Deposit solid human waste inside catholes at least 6 to 8 inches deep and near the campsite

 

    • Ensure that all trash and food are packed away when leaving the campsite

 

    • When washing dishes, make sure to use minimal amount of biodegradable soap  




    1. Leave what you find




    • Do not bring home any wildlife specimens

 

    • Refrain from touching historical and natural structures in order to preserve them

 

    • Do not build structures or dig trenches




    1. Minimize campfire impacts




    • Keep the campfire small

 

    • Always put out the campfire completely, and burn the wood and coal to ash and scatter them once cooled

 

    • Use existing fire rings, fire pans, and mound fires




    1. Respect Wildlife




    • Do not feed wild animals

 

    • Do not follow wild animals as they can feel threatened or become startled

 

    • If you have your pets with you, strictly monitor them and avoid them interacting with wild animals




    1. Be considerate of others




    • Avoid producing loud noises

 

    • Respect other visitors and treat them how you would like to be treated

 

    • Always be courteous

bodies.content:
Going camping is an exciting and rewarding experience. But the key to success when camping is to make sure you’re prepared for anything that might come your way. To help make your camping trip a success, here is a comprehensive camping checklist of all of the items you might need.

 

Tent and sleeping equipment: This is the most important part of your camping setup. Make sure you have a quality tent, sleeping bags, and pillows for everyone. If you’re heading out for a multi-night trip, consider bringing an air mattress or cot to make sleeping much more comfortable.

 

Clothing and Footwear: Depending on the time of year and the climate you’ll be camping in, make sure you have the right clothing and footwear. This includes hats, gloves, thick socks, and a good pair of boots. Don’t forget to bring an extra set of clothes in case of rain or other inclement weather.

 

Cooking Supplies: Camping cooking supplies should also be a priority. Bring some quality pots, pans, and utensils, as well as a cutting board, paper towels, and any tools you might need. Don’t forget to bring the fuel for your stove.

 

First Aid Kit: Accidents can happen, so make sure you bring along a first aid kit, filled with the necessary supplies for any minor medical issues that might arise.

 

Lights: Make sure you’re prepared for when the sun goes down by bringing flashlights, lanterns, and extra batteries.

 

Hygiene and Sanitation Supplies: Hygiene is important when camping, so make sure you bring some hand sanitiser, wet wipes, soap, a washcloth, a toothbrush, toothpaste, and any medications you might need.

 

Maps and Navigation Tools: Bring along a quality map and compass, as well as a GPS navigation device. These will help you stay on the right path if you decide to venture out on a hike or explore your surroundings.

 

Miscellaneous: Bring along a few miscellaneous items, such as bug spray, a multi-tool, and a water filter.

 

By keeping this camping checklist handy, you’ll be able to make sure you have everything you need for your next camping trip. A little bit of preparation can go a long way in ensuring your outing is a success.

article.title: Proper Preparations for a Hike

bodies.content:
Before embarking on any hike, it is important to be well-prepared. Here are some tips to ensure a safe and enjoyable outing:

  1. Research the area you're hiking before departure - know the dangers and potential route changes that may await you. Take into account local weather patterns, wildlife activity and trail conditions to determine the safest time to go.
  2. Dress appropriately for the weather and terrain. Wear sturdy shoes with good traction. Bring plenty of food and water with you - remember to drink plenty of water to stay hydrated and pack energy snacks for when you're on the trail.
  3. Know the limitations of your own physical capabilities. Be realistic about your level of fitness and don't try to push yourself too far too fast. As with any physical activity, it's important to gradually build up your endurance to prevent injury. Consult with a physician if you have any questions about your health or fitness level before starting a strenuous workout program.
  4. Leave details of your hike itinerary with someone at home and make sure they know how and when to contact you in an emergency. This is especially important if you plan to go alone.
  5. Carry emergency supplies, such as a map and compass, flashlight and extra batteries, first aid kit, cell phone charger, water and food.
  6. Plan ahead and never set out without enough supplies and water to survive a night in the woods. A good rule of thumb is to bring twice as much as you think you'll need for your trek. Remember to bring rain gear and/or extra clothing to keep you warm and dry if necessary. Hiking can be very exhilarating but it can also be dangerous if you're not prepared. 
  7. Have fun and stay alert at all times! Don't allow yourself to become distracted by all the sights and sounds around you. Take your time and enjoy your surroundings; you never know what interesting discoveries you might make during your adventure!

article.title: The Skills you need to do outdoor camping in the Philippines

bodies.content:
If you’re planning a camping trip in the Philippines, there are certain skills you’ll need to make sure you have a successful and enjoyable adventure. From planning out your route to knowing how to build a campfire, outdoors camping in the Philippines requires knowledge, preparation and practical skills.

 

Before you hit the road, make sure to have a sound plan and the right supplies. Make sure you know the terrain you’ll be facing, the conditions of your designated campsite and the types of activities you’ll be doing. That way, you can pack the right kind of gear, clothes, and supplies. Additionally, make sure to have a detailed map of the area and directions to your destination.

 

Additionally, you’ll need a basic knowledge of first aid, as well as knowledge of how to survive in the wilderness. Make sure to bring the necessary supplies for first aid, like bandages, antiseptic wipes, medications, and a camping first aid kit. Additionally, you’ll need to know how to build a fire, identify edible plants, and use a compass.

 

And of course, you’ll need to know how to set up and break down a campsite. A successful camping trip requires you to know how to properly set up a tent. Make sure you know proper tent setup for the conditions and terrain you’ll be facing. Additionally, make sure you know how to properly pack and store your supplies, how to build a fire pit, and how to keep the campsite clean and safe.

 

Finally, the right attitude is key. Make sure to stay positive, enjoy yourself, and respect the nature around you. Be prepared to encounter wild animals, insects, and other items that can be uncomfortable or unsettling. Be aware of your surroundings, and ensure that you’re being safe and responsible.

 

Camping in the Philippines can be an unforgettable and rewarding experience, but you’ll need to have the right set of skills to make sure it’s a success. From knowledge of first aid and wilderness survival, to proper tent setup and campfire building, these skills will help you navigate the outdoor world and have the most enjoyable experience possible.
